meta.title: Gram Urja: village energy, from 0 to 1
meta.description: Learn how a village can move to clean energy, and the skills that make it work. Readings, scenarios, quizzes and a 0 to 1 view for biogas and solar.

supportAcknowledgement: Gram Urja is supported by the Heinrich Boell Stiftung.
footer: Gram Urja is a learning tool for village energy transitions. Content adapted from the Green Skill directory for rural Haryana. Details of schemes, prices and courses change, so always confirm them.

home.title: How does a village get from <zero>0</zero> to <one>1</one> on clean energy?
home.lead: Not with a machine alone. With a need, some numbers, an agreement, and people who have the skills to build it and keep it working. Learn it, try it, then plan it together.

feed.title: Try the numbers: is there enough dung?
feed.prompt: Move the slider to the number of cattle in a household.
feed.caption: About {{kg}} kg of dung a day, against the ≈50 kg a 2 m³ plant typically needs.
feed.good: This is about what a 2 m³ household plant is typically fed. Next: check what can really be collected each day, in every season.
feed.mid: The directory says households with 3 or more cattle can consider a plant, but a 2 m³ plant is usually fed by 4–5 animals. Ask a trained mason, or think about sharing with a neighbour.
feed.low: This is well short of what a small plant usually needs. Households like this can pool dung through an SHG, or join a community plant.
feed.fine: A rough rule, worked out from the directory’s figure of about 50 kg a day for 4–5 animals. Real amounts depend on the animals, feed and how much dung is actually collected.

sub.title: Try the numbers: how much subsidy for a rooftop?
sub.prompt: PM Surya Ghar, as the directory describes it. Move the slider to the size of the system.
sub.caption: Subsidy: {{amount}}
sub.over: The subsidy stops at 3 kW (₹78,000). Anything bigger gets no extra subsidy, so every extra kW is paid in full.
sub.cap: At 3 kW the subsidy reaches its cap of ₹78,000.
sub.base: The first 2 kW get ₹30,000 per kW. The band from 2 to 3 kW gets ₹18,000 per kW.
sub.fine: Rates are as given in the directory. Confirm current amounts on the official portal or with HAREDA before deciding.

sceneDetail.schematic: How the system connects · schematic, not an installation plan
sceneDetail.caution: The scene illustrates a possible arrangement. Installation alone does not guarantee income, crop growth or reliable service.

biogas.description: Cross-section of a fixed-dome biogas plant: mixing tank, sealed digester with gas headspace, gas pipe and valve, condensate drain, stove, outlet chamber and slurry collection.
biogas.before: First, understand demand, secure inputs, agree responsibilities and prepare trained people. The operating flows appear once the plant is shown in use.
biogas.allDetail: 1. Collectable dung feeds the plant. 2. Gas goes to the kitchen. 3. Slurry has a separate route to agricultural use. Each connection needs people and an operating arrangement.
biogas.inputDetail: The aggregator and operator organise reliable collection and daily feeding. Cattle count alone does not tell you how much dung can actually reach the plant.
biogas.energyDetail: Gas leaves the digester through a separate connection to the kitchen. Trained operators and qualified maintenance support are needed to keep the service working.
biogas.outputDetail: Slurry leaves through the outlet. Handling, processing and arrangements with farmers need planning; crop benefits and sales are not automatic.

solar.description: Solar irrigation system: PV array, pump controller, separate electrical cable and rising water main, submersible pump, water storage tank and irrigation outlet.
solar.before: First, assess energy and water needs, choose an appropriate site and prepare the installation team. A demonstration is followed by an operating pump arrangement.
solar.allDetail: 1. Sunlight reaches the panels. 2. Electricity passes through a controller to the pump. 3. Water travels in a separate pipe. Rooftop solar is a separate application.
solar.inputDetail: Panels convert sunlight into electrical energy. Site assessment considers sunlight and shading; the diagram does not predict output.
solar.energyDetail: The electrical connection powers the pump through its controller. Qualified installers and maintenance technicians handle technical work. Rooftop solar alone does not imply outage backup.
solar.outputDetail: The pump moves available water to irrigation. Water assessment, access rules and sustainable use remain necessary; solar power does not create groundwater.

engineering.scope: One reference arrangement is shown. Dimensions, gas treatment, electrical protection and controls must be specified for the site. Animated flows show direction, not speed or output.

biogas.title: Fixed-dome biogas plant
notes: Feed: collected dung is mixed with water before entering the sealed digester.
Digestion: microbes break down material without oxygen; biogas collects above the slurry.
Gas: a separate pipe carries gas through a valve to the appliance; condensate needs managed drainage.
Displacement: gas pressure moves slurry into the outlet chamber. Overflow goes to collection for managed use.

solar.title: Solar-powered irrigation
notes: Capture: PV modules convert sunlight into electricity. Output varies with sunlight, temperature and shading.
Control: a compatible pump controller regulates motor operation; protection and earthing are part of the installation.
Lift: a submerged pump lifts groundwater through the rising main. Required power depends on flow and total head.
Use: stored water supplies irrigation. Tank-level and dry-run controls, water availability and extraction limits need planning.
